He orchestrates the final and most terrible fulfilment of the ancient enmity between the seed of the woman (Eve) and the seed of the serpent (Satan), first declared in Genesis 3:15. In the latter days he rises to power among the ten kings of the fourth empire — the final world kingdom prophesied in Daniel 2 & 7 that will exist in the last days. He subdues three of those ten kings and establishes his dominion over the remaining seven kings and over that empire. He is the concentrated expression of Satan’s rebellion — a man raised up and empowered by the dragon, yet strictly limited by the sovereign permission of Almighty God. His nature is proud and arrogant; his character is marked by deceit, lawlessness, and a deep hatred for God’s people. His sole aim is to usurp the worship that belongs to Christ alone and to make war against God's people. In the end, this proud and blasphemous figure will be destroyed by the returning Lord Jesus, the Messiah. The head of the serpent and his seed will be crushed by the Seed of the woman (Genesis 3:15; Revelation 19:19-21; Daniel 7:11, 26).

Abomination of Desolation This is a term used by Jesus to describe a time of terrible desecration of the holy place (Jerusalem). It coincides with great Tribulation (troubles/persecution) against God's people, particularly in Judea. This exact phrase is also used in the book of Daniel 11:31 when a Greek General, Antiochus IV, descrated the altar in Jerusalem by sacrificing a pig in 167 BC. Historical details of this are recorded in the Jewish books of the Maccabees. This was prophesied by Daniel about 350 years before it happened. Antiochus removed the daily sacrifices, there was great deception and terrible persecution of the Jews. All these events are prophesied to happen again in Daniel 9:27, shortly before the Messiah returns to reign. A biblical definition of 'Abomination' is found in Pro 6:16-19: Seven things Yahweh hates, Yes, they are an abomination to Him: 1. A proud look, 2. A lying tongue, 3. Hands that shed innocent blood, 4. A heart that devises wicked plans, 5. Feet that are swift in running to evil, 6. A false witness who speaks lies, 7. And one who sows discord among brethren. These are the characteristics of the Beast's behaviour, but be aware that he initially may come across as good! However, He lies, deceives and accuses others; possibly of the very evil that he commits.

Definition: Torah (God's ways) Torah refers to the first 5 books of the bible, from Genesis to Deuteronomy. It is the period that covers the formation of God's chosen people into the nation Israel up to when they enter the promised land. The term Torah covers: 3 Covenants They promise the restoration of mankind's dominion over the earth. The covenants were made with Noah, Abraham, and then with Israel at Mount Sinai. Torah's covenants also point to the Messiah finally ruling the world with perfect righteousness and justice. God's instructions How to love God and each other. Torah is Yahweh's universal law. Seven annual festivals They represent scriptural principles of Redemption, Resurrection and Eternal Life with God. (Just like church stained glass windows were pictorial representations of scripture, God's feasts give insights into prophecy and princples through the experience of the rituals.) Examples of Yahweh’s Torah: Temple feasts, rituals and practises represent spiritual principles. • The feast of Passover is a picture of Christ’s death as a substitution for our death from our sin, just like the Passover lamb was a substitution for the first born. •The food laws are principles of how things set apart for God are holy and are contaminated by things which are not clean. Therefore they are no longer holy. They give examples of what God considers both clean and unclean. • Eg the life is in the blood and is not to be eaten. Human life is precious and is not to be taken. • The principle of not mixing things which do not go together: a) Wool and linen - wool keeps you warm and linen keeps you cool b) Sowing grain in a vineyard (self explanatory) c) Do not plough with a donkey and ox together - donkeys buck at the yoke to go faster and oxen want to pull heavy loads slow and steady • In the NT, Paul used the principle of not mixing to teach, ‘do not be unequally yoked to unbelievers’. Discovering Truth in Torah When reading God’s Torah, look for principles that you can apply in your life rather than the ‘legalistic letter of the law’. In addition to reading Torah, meditation combined with participation in the Torah instructions (as far as is sensible and practical), results in new revelations of God, His ways and His prophetic events; eg Passover events map on to Jesus’ triumphal entry into Jerusalem, His resurrection and the journey to the Promised Land and first fruits. It is the first of three harvest feasts and harvest is relation to resurrection.
